teaser.text: ServiceNow sells cloud software that organizes work inside large organizations, from a broken laptop to a customer problem. Its business rests on a shared platform, recurring subscriptions, and the effort required to keep customers’ processes running.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for ServiceNow?

paragraphs.text: The company’s FY26 guidance implies an approximately 18% cash-after-stock-pay margin. The base case starts near that level and improves gradually as productivity offsets delivery costs. The bear case assumes weaker growth and margins below guidance, while the bull case reaches a 22.5% margin by the final date. The bull case is supported by ServiceNow AI exceeding $1 billion of annual contract value in Q2 2026, but ACV does not yet prove broad renewal expansion.

blocks.heading: How much cash does ServiceNow really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation is the largest recurring reason cash flow exceeds profit. Deducting $1,955 million of stock pay from free cash flow leaves $2,578 million of “real free cash flow”, an analytical allowance for the cost of employee ownership rather than a GAAP line. Its margin rose from 11.2% in 2021 to 19.4% in 2025, showing that cash generation improved even after this charge.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for ServiceNow today?

paragraphs.text: At $138.61 a share, the market values the company at $143,303.61 million. A trailing P/E compares the price with earnings from the last twelve months; a forward P/E compares it with forecast earnings. The two figures are 86.6x and 27.6x. The forecast implies approximately $5.02 of earnings per share, but the comparison is useful only if both measures count profit in the same way.

blocks.heading: Did ServiceNow keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The company has delivered against guidance, with qualifications. Its October 2025 outlook called for annual subscription revenue of US$12.835–12.845 billion. The reported result was US$12.883 billion. In July 2026, Gina Mastantuono again reported results above guidance, while noting that some federal revenue had shifted forward from the following quarter. Timing and currency therefore matter when judging execution.

blocks.heading: How have ServiceNow revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: Total revenue growth eased from 30.5% in 2021 to 20.9% in 2025. Subscription revenue grew approximately 21.0% in 2025, while constant-currency growth was 20%. Constant currency translates both years at comparable exchange rates, so a stronger euro does not look like extra software sold. Q2 2026 subscription growth was 24.5% as reported and 23% in constant currency, making the latter the cleaner starting point for judging demand.

June 2026 exposed the difference between operating economics and bottom-line profit. Subscription gross margin fell to 73% from 80%. Operating income was $162 million, while net income was $298 million, supported by investment gains of $273 million and a California tax benefit of $51 million. The adjusted measures and tax bridge belong beside the reported results.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in ServiceNow’s next results?

paragraphs.text: Investors should compare subscription and cRPO growth with the Q3 outlook and listen to management’s explanation of federal demand. A slower Q3 revenue figure could reflect the earlier pull-forward; weaker contract growth alongside it would be more troubling.
